title: Context router predicts continuous Mirror code
hypothesis: A learned linear context-to-code router over one shared nonlinear block will recover held-out task functions with less actual payload than a same-dimension generic hypernetwork and a discrete prototype router, without worse query quality.
physical_object: one fixed shared tanh nonlinear block
mirror_coordinate: two continuous coefficients (scale, shift) predicted from a fixed four-value context sketch
logical_multiplicity: one logical nonlinear function per context
controls: discrete K=8 prototype router from MA-453

task.context: mean(x), mean(y), mean(x*y), mean(y^2) from support only

allowed: choose one shared context normalization variant among raw and per-world standardized
development.selection_metric: mean dev query NRMSE subject to serialized bytes and query compute reported

success_gate: On every fresh world, continuous Mirror routing improves NRMSE by at least 10% over discrete K=8 routing, and at N=20 payload is no larger than both discrete routing and generic hypernetwork; report independent fit as upper control.
failure_gate: Generic hypernetwork matches/beats Mirror at equal or fewer bytes, discrete routing matches at equal/fewer bytes, Mirror misses per-world quality gate, or learned router fails to beat the no-adaptation baseline.
boundaries: Context contains support-derived summary features; no task ID or teacher coefficients exposed.
Does not establish transformer or natural multi-task performance.
